Arab Kings.
Now there had been present at that defeat along with Jekermish a certain man of the people of Mosul whose name was Abu Talib ibn Kusairat,
and he had fled to Arbela. Jawali demanded him from Ibn Musak, the lord of Arbela,
that he should send him to him.
And when he was sent,
Jawali released the son of the lord of Arbela,
who had also been a prisoner with him.
Then Ibn Kusairat, when he came to Jawali, promised him that he would surrender Mosul to him,
and would collect for him a wealth of gold from places that he knew.
And he kept him with him in honor.
Now the judge of Mosul, whose name was Ibn Wad'an,
because there was enmity between him and Ibn Kusairat,
sent to Jawali
and promised that he would surrender Mosul,
if he would kill Ibn Kusairat.
And when he granted him his request and sent him the head of his enemy,
the Turks who were in Mosul were distressed at what Ibn Wad'an had done,
and they rushed upon him and killed him.
And thus, within a few days, evil was repaid for evil.
And in those days, Qilij Arslan arrived from the territory of the Romans at Jazirat Qardu (Jazirat Ibn 'Umar).
And Jawali abandoned [the siege] and fled, and went and plundered the city of Balad,
and moved toward Syria.
And Qilij Arslan came against Mosul,
and easily took control of it.
And he did not harm Zangi the son of Jekermish,
nor those who were with him,
nor anyone of the people of the city.
Rather, he commanded
that anyone who should slander anyone before him
should surely die.
And he reinstated the judge 'Ubaydallah ibn Qasim of Shahrazur once again to his post.
And he abolished the proclamation of Sultan Muhammad from Mosul,
and they proclaimed him [Qilij Arslan] after the Caliph.
And he placed in the fortress of Mosul a man whose name was Bazmish.
And he left his son Malik-Shah, who was eleven years old, there in Mosul and proclaimed him king,
and also the boy's own mother beside him in the palace.
And he himself marched towards the Khabur,
and with him were five thousand horsemen.
Now the emir Jawali allied himself with Ridwan, the lord of Aleppo,
and gathered four thousand horsemen,
who were, however, brave and valiant men;
and they came and met Qilij Arslan on the Khabur.
And when battle was joined,
Qilij Arslan displayed great valor,
for he entered into the midst of the ranks
